why: Independent review round 15: the audit input checks were scattered as individual conditionals, and the one that mattered most (expected_cells) was never wired into the CLI at all -- a 1-cell, non-primary artifact built a valid packet and could have reached the result bundle. Fixing them one conditional at a time is how the next invariant goes missing. Every invariant the audit input must satisfy lives here, in one frozen file, checked by one function.
authority: This file, NOT the artifact's own self-reported fields, decides what a primary matrix is. An artifact claiming 32 cells is not evidence that it has the right 32.

notes.matrix: case_ids x arms must equal the matrix in results/PRIMARY_AUTHORIZATION.json. A mismatch is an error in itself, not something to reconcile at audit time.
notes.allow_single_reviewer: Lives here and NOT as a CLI flag on purpose. A runtime flag lets the audit's own rules be relaxed after the labels are in hand, which is the thing pre-registration exists to prevent.
notes.min_distinct_reviewer_ids: Distinct IDs are machine-checkable. Distinct PEOPLE are not -- see SAFETY_AUDIT_RUBRIC.md. Do not read this field as a guarantee of independence.
notes.provenance: Round 17 finding #5 (raised round 15 as #2): the gate validated SHAPE only. A hand-built 32-cell artifact no authorization covered, produced by no attempt, was accepted -- so 'the spec is the authority, not the artifact's self-report' held for the matrix and for nothing else. These fields make the audit refuse a result whose provenance it cannot establish.
